title: Proverbs 14
paragraphs: ¹ A wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands. ² Whoever walks in integrity fears the LORD, but whoever takes crooked paths despises him. ³ A fool's mouth is a rod of arrogance, but the lips of the wise protect them. ⁴ Where there are no oxen, the stall is clean — but large harvests come from the strength of the ox. ⁵ An honest witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.

⁶ A mocker seeks wisdom but finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning. ⁷ Stay away from a fool, for you will not learn anything from them. ⁸ The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way, but the folly of fools is deception. ⁹ Fools mock at making amends for sin, but goodwill is found among the upright. ¹⁰ The heart knows its own bitterness, and no outsider can share in its joy.

¹¹ The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish. ¹² There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death. ¹³ Even in laughter the heart may ache, and rejoicing may end in grief. ¹⁴ The faithless will have their fill of their own ways, and the good person will be satisfied from their own. ¹⁵ A simple person believes anything, but the prudent weighs every step.

¹⁶ The wise fear the LORD and turn away from evil, but a fool rushes ahead recklessly. ¹⁷ A quick-tempered person acts foolishly, and one who schemes is hated. ¹⁸ The simple inherit folly, but the discerning are crowned with knowledge. ¹⁹ Evildoers will bow before the good, and the wicked will bow at the gates of the righteous. ²⁰ The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.

²¹ Whoever despises their neighbor sins, but happy is whoever shows kindness to the poor. ²² Do not those who plan evil go astray? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good. ²³ In all hard work there is profit, but idle talk leads only to poverty. ²⁴ The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the foolishness of fools is their folly. ²⁵ A truthful witness saves lives, but a false witness is a fraud.

²⁶ Whoever fears the LORD has a secure fortress, and their children will have a refuge. ²⁷ The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death. ²⁸ A large population is a king's glory, but without subjects a prince is ruined. ²⁹ Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding, but a quick temper exalts folly. ³⁰ A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

³¹ Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God. ³² The wicked are brought down by their own wickedness, but even in death the righteous have a refuge. ³³ Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but what is inside a fool is plain for all to see. ³⁴ Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people. ³⁵ The king's favor comes to a servant who acts wisely, but his anger falls on the one who acts shamefully.
